subject: Throughput charter & SLO clarifications for FleetAI integration
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Turner <sam.turner@fleetai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Throughput charter & SLO clarifications for FleetAI integration

Hi Sam —

Great to meet earlier. Quick write-up from our side to capture what we heard and the specific data points we'll need to produce a preliminary sizing and SLO proposal. Please correct anything I misunderstood.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary integration: streaming generation for driver-facing summaries + batch reranking for route optimization.
- Desired SLOs: low-latency streaming to devices (target p95 per-chunk < 300–400ms), and batch rerank p95 < 1s for 1–2k items.
- Traffic pattern: steady-state traffic from nightly jobs + daytime interactive streams during peak hours.

Concrete asks (what we need from you)
1) Steady-state tokens/sec and expected peak burst (tokens/sec and duration)
2) Typical prompt length (tokens) and average output length (tokens) for streaming and batch flows
3) Concurrency: expected number of simultaneous streaming connections during peak minute and sustained concurrency
4) Chunking: average chunk size you expect clients to accept (characters/tokens) and whether you need chunk-level determinism
5) Any enforced per-request time budgets or early-abort policies from the FleetAI side
6) Whether you require server-side function-calling or structured outputs (JSON) for downstream parsing

We attached a short sample_measurement_template.csv to make it easy to drop in numbers — will turn this into a sizing after we get your numbers.

Proposed next steps
- If you can populate the template, send back by EOD Wed (Dec 2) and we'll have a preliminary Dedicated sizing and a hosted fallback plan by Friday.
- If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min technical follow-up to walk through prefix caching and streaming chunk sizing tradeoffs.

Thanks — looking forward to the numbers.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Sam Turner <sam.turner@fleetai.com>

Cc: Ops Team <infraops@fleetai.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput charter & SLO clarifications for FleetAI integration

Sergio — thanks for the clear list. Confirming numbers from our telemetry (last 30 days) below. I pasted the CSV snapshot as well and attached the full dump.

Summary numbers (telemetry window average / peaks):
- Steady-state tokens/sec: ~120,000 tokens/sec (this is our daytime baseline for all devices)
- Peak sustained: 1,200,000 tokens/sec (observed for ~20-30 minutes during regional morning surge)
- Burst ceiling: up to ~2,000,000 tokens/sec for short spikes (1–10 minutes) during incidents or major routing updates
- Average prompt size (streaming): 40 tokens; average generated length per request: 180 tokens
- Average prompt size (batch rerank): 90 tokens input, 15 tokens output per item
- Concurrency: up to ~480 simultaneous streaming connections at global peak; sustained peak-minute concurrency ~320
- Chunking: clients can accept ~128–256 token chunk sizes; we prefer fewer, larger chunks to reduce overhead
- Determinism: not strict — eventual completeness is more important than exact chunk timing; however p95 per-chunk latency target is useful for UX
- Function calling: yes, some workflows require structured JSON outputs for downstream ingestion (schema v2 attached)

Attachment: fleetai_workload_snapshot.csv (30-day window)

We can share a HubSpot note (HS-5421) with the metrics export if you want raw telemetry. Happy to hop on a tech call Thurs or Fri.

—Sam
Sam Turner
Platform Engineering Lead, FleetAI
sam.turner@fleetai.com

Subject: Re: Throughput charter & SLO clarifications for FleetAI integration

Thanks Sam — this is very helpful. A few quick follow-ups from the infra/sizing side so we can be more concrete with recommendations: 

1) Chunking tradeoffs: if you can tolerate 200–256 token chunks, that maps well to a batching strategy where we can amortize kernel launch time and improve GPU utilization. If you prefer <100 token chunks, we'll surface a quantized-latency plan with dedicated lower-N model variants.

2) Burst handling: do you have a hard budget for how many bursts you want Redwood Dedicated to absorb vs. falling back to hosted/elastic? e.g., reserve for 1.2M steady peak and allow hosted fallback for 2M+ incidents, or reserve more headroom?

3) Prefix/personalization cache: are prompts heavily personalized per user (low reuse) or do you see common templates (high reuse)? High reuse lets us rely on prefix caching to drop token cost significantly.

4) Function-calling schema: please share the v2 schema sample you mentioned and whether you need validation at generation time (we can add a small validation microservice in the pipeline).

Attached is a short Redwood prelim sizing estimate that maps your steady/peak numbers to a recommended Dedicated profile and an explanation of expected p95 latency by model class. This is preliminary — we'll refine after the CSV.

If it's useful, I'll block 30 minutes Thursday at 10am PT for a quick tech sync (Sergio — can you confirm?) and we can walk through the sizing PDF and caching options.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0210

Marissa / Sergio —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. I've uploaded the full export and a cleaned snapshot to the Drive link below and attached the small CSV extract for quick reference. A couple answers inline: 

- Burst handling: we'd prefer Redwood to guarantee sizing up to 1.2M tokens/sec and have hosted fallback for >1.2M spikes. For critical pushes (release-day routing updates) we can pre-schedule extra capacity, but those are rare (once per quarter).
- Prefix reuse: roughly 60% of streaming prompts are templated (high reuse); 40% are per-driver personalization. So caching will help but not eliminate load.
- Validation: we need a lightweight schema validation at generation time for the JSON outputs (reject or flag failures).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fleetai-snapshot
HubSpot: HS-5421 (shared note with telemetry)

We'll take the 30-min slot Thursday at 10am PT — please send calendar invite and a short agenda (we'll include infra and product folks). Looking forward to the preliminary sizing.
